findings: Conversion is intentionally non-destructive: create a private linked counterpart and retain the original canonical Task/Note and history. Notes remain in legacy canonical APIs; no new Markdown store or synchronization engine. This choice is explicit in confirmation/UI.

Task-to-Note refuses active rewarded/pending/recurring Tasks until a separate archive policy. Accepted past rewards are neither repeated nor reversed; a real native completion/grant fixture verifies original Task/history/ledger/users unchanged. Note-to-Task creates fresh private unfinished Task without due/assignee/reward and refuses oversized text without truncation.

Two actual native failures showed unrelated Note edits and shared snapshot restore deleting typed links through FK cascade; a third missing-row error followed that failed restoration. The existing users retained-ID write path now also upserts Notes and deletes only removed IDs, inside the same gateway. Actual canonical Note deletion still prunes only its own links.

An actual Chromium revocation test showed a disabled button still exposing a revoked Note title even though the API returned an empty authorized list. Rendering now filters current peer scope before labels and re-fetches on current Note IDs; original no-title assertion remains.

One parent Collaboration actor bootstrap stopped in privacy cleanup before Member UI, with native HTTP200 and no functional-page assertion reached. The failed DOM/network/trace and read-only diagnostic run are retained. All eighteen final journeys pass first-attempt on clean owned fixtures. This does not claim a production auth fix.
